messages:
Ellie: Day 3 check-in — did local dev setup, followed the quickstart, launched the model-serving demo. Blocker: can't reach the internal npm registry (requests time out).

Sam: @Ellie can you paste the exact error? is it a DNS failure or TCP timeout?

Ellie: It's a TCP timeout when `npm install` tries to fetch from registry.internal.redwood. DNS resolves fine. Example: 
```
npm WARN registry request to https://registry.internal.redwood/some-package failed, reason: connect ETIMEDOUT
```

Ava: Hmm — we've seen MTU issues from some VPNs cause that. Can you try `traceroute registry.internal.redwood` and paste output? Also try `curl -v` to the registry URL.

Ellie: traceroute output: 
```
traceroute to registry.internal.redwood (10.10.8.2), 30 hops max
 1 10.2.0.1  1.12 ms  0.98 ms  0.91 ms
 2 192.0.2.1  15.3 ms  16.2 ms  15.1 ms
 3 * * *
```

Sam: Looks like packets drop after our edge. Quick workaround: set MTU lower on your VPN interface (e.g., `sudo ip link set dev tun0 mtu 1400`) or enable TCP MTU probing: `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`.

Priya: :thumbsup: I had this on Day 2 — lowering MTU fixed `npm` for me. Also, if you need a quick install, try `npm_config_registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/ npm install` to pull from public mirror while infra investigates.

onboarding-bot: Welcome Ellie! Don't forget the "Networking 101" session at 4pm today in #eng-platform — useful for VPN quirks.

Ellie: Thanks all — will try MTU tweak and the public-registry fallback. 4pm pairing with @Priya works if I still need help. Will update after tests.

Sam: I'll open a netops ticket referencing this traceroute and ping the colo team. If you can, DM me the output of `ip a` and `cat /proc/net/if_inet6` (if IPv6 present) so we have details.

Ellie: Got it — sending DM now. Thanks! :smile:
